title: THE OPENING PACED UP: the landing as one shot, the dog on two near points
context: The owner's playtest notes, 2026-11-12 evening: 1) "isao landing, the camera focus jumps too many time; focus on the rocket, no cuts, it opens, isao comes out." 2) "dog recon beginning is cute but much too slow; we accellerate for now, maybe reduce to scouting two spots, much closer, rather than 3 far apart." Branch opening-pace from 5c6d3b52 (the recon dog and the economy merged), unpushed. Target given: the Rotor's seat at about 70-80 s from the deploy instead of ~141-149 s.
outcome: BUILT. The cuts from the touchdown to the dog's seat were eight: the rail round the nose to Isao's arc (its look point moved ~35 m in 2.7 s), the cut to his face on a 20 degree lens, the glide into the landers' tour (10.4 s), the snap to the orbit camera, the cut into the K9's print close-up and its three angle cuts, the snap back, the cut to the chase. Now from the touchdown (flown or automatic; the flight's side view unchanged) the camera eases 2.5 s into a held framing of the rocket (STORY_ARRIVAL.hold, src/fx/arrival.js holdAt: look 20 m up the hull, eye 54 -> 46 m over 16 s, the game's 68 degree lens) and stays through the door, Isao's climb and arc (door 0.8 s after touchdown, climb 1.5 s, arc 1.6 s; he grows to his game size on it) and his three lines ('arrivalTalk' on the same pose). The swap to the salvage waits until the rocket is out of the frame or under 8 % of its height (arrival.swapHeld; foundry-fx holds the AFR-01's events; 60 s bound). On the dog's opening (arrival `hand`) the landers' tour is dropped (kept on ?settle=N): a yielding hold (camera-shot `yields`, busy()) that the K9's print eases out of (camera-shot from/easeIn, 3.5 s), the K9's own print 7.2 s on one wide angle at the game's lens ending on a yielding printHold, the chase easing out of it (2.4 s); with nothing to take the hold, playGlide eases into the orbit camera. The dog: DOG_SCOUT points 2 at 5-7 hops, 50-80 degrees apart (pickPoints spreadMax), ROCK AND CRYSTALS then BIOMASS, survey 1.5 s, drive.sprint 6.5 m/s, recall 40 s, pay 150 kg a point. Measured (--dog-scout, real keys, story clock): print asked 0.4, seat 7.9 (was 26.4), surveys 24.6 / 40.2 (45.3 / 75.4 / 109.1), home 47.0 (128.3), gate 52.7 (134.8), Rotor 63.6 (138.3), the Rotor's seat 66.9, 66.4 s after the deploy (141.5), wave cleared 73.9 (160.2), the card 124.9 (205.7). DOG BUDGET: salvage 1,800, surveys 2,100 (2,250), the rover poured 320 (323), the card 2,420 (2,573), after the card 1,570 (1,723).
alternatives: Keep the face close-up for the talk and hide the swap behind it: a cut, which the note forbids; the swap now waits for the frame instead.

Move the landers' tour later (before the dog's print or at the expedition): it is a cutaway in the span and the expedition already shows the sites; dropped from the dog's opening, kept on ?settle=N, the owner's call whether it comes back somewhere.
Points at 6-8 hops to land the seat inside 70-80 s for the bot: the bot drives straighter than a player; 5-7 left in content for the playtest.
One opening shot owned by a single module across the arrival, the print and the dog's seat: chained eased shots with yielding holds keep the three hosts apart.
evidence: scripts/browser-lock.sh node scripts/browser-test.mjs --dog-scout: PASS 10 on e0cd037c; DOG TIMELINE (story clock) print asked 0.42, K9 print 0.71, seat 7.86, surveys 24.56 / 40.2, home 47.02, gate 52.68, Rotor 63.61, tremor 64.24, the Rotor's seat 66.85 (66.4 after the deploy), wave cleared 73.94, depot 98.38, rover home and THE FIRST ORDERS 124.88, Stålheart print 125.26, construction 137.67, second Rotor 139.1; DOG BUDGET landing 0, salvage 1800, surveys 2100, wave laid 433, field at the flare 352, poured 320, card 2420, after the card 1570; the camera from the touchdown to the seat 805 frames over 20.1 s (arrival > arrivalTalk > arrivalHold > petPrint > dogScout), largest steps 1.2 m / 3.8 m / 3.9 deg, no cut.
